t: You're at the Royal Free Hospital, a major teaching hospital in Hampstead. Several writers and journalists died here. Bernice Rubens, who in 1970 became the first woman to win the Booker Prize, for The Elected Member, died here. So did the biographer Joanna Richardson and the journalist Nora Beloff, who in 1964 became the first woman political correspondent on a British newspaper. Ray Strachey, the feminist, and the BBC broadcaster Serajur Rahman also died here, as did Sarah Kyolaba, the last surviving wife of Idi Amin, who ran a restaurant and then a hair salon in England.
